# Maintenance request.
Report a repair or building issue in a CenterPoint-managed association. We confirm receipt, assess responsibility, and coordinate the right vendor.

**Emergency?** Do not use this form. For flooding, fire, a gas smell, or an elevator entrapment, call [773.728.0652](tel:+17737280652). If anyone is in danger, call 911 first.

## Report a repair.
Tell us what is wrong and where. Photos help; attach them to the email that opens.

- **[773.728.0652](tel:+17737280652)** Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM

- **[service@centerpointmgmt.com](mailto:service@centerpointmgmt.com)** Replies within one business day

- **5107 N Western Ave, Suite 1S** Chicago, IL 60625

## How maintenance requests are handled.
Each request is logged and reviewed by management. We confirm who is responsible under your declaration, then schedule the association's vendor for common elements or let you know if the repair is an owner responsibility. If entry to your unit is needed, we contact you first using the details you provide.

Not sure whether a repair belongs to you or the association? The declaration decides, and the answer is often different for windows, balconies, plumbing, and appliances. Our guide to [owner versus association repairs in Illinois](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/blog/condo-repairs-owner-vs-association-illinois) explains the usual lines, and our team can confirm the answer for your building.

See how we coordinate [building maintenance and vendors](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/services/maintenance-coordination) for the associations we manage.

## Common questions.

### What counts as an emergency?
Active water leaks, flooding, fire or smoke, a gas smell, no heat in freezing weather, and elevator entrapments. Call [773.728.0652](tel:+17737280652) instead of using this form, and call 911 if anyone is in danger.

### Who pays for the repair?
It depends on your declaration. Common elements are usually the association's responsibility; many items inside a unit belong to the owner. We confirm before work is scheduled.

### I rent my unit. Can my tenant submit a request?
Yes. Tenants can use this form for building and common-area issues. Repairs inside the unit generally go through the unit owner.
